task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 12, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about Plover Reed Flowers' standing restaurant orders and the choices a grower makes between dependable small deliveries and higher-priced occasional work.

facts.text: An Aug. 12, 2026, field note records grower Nessa Sorn separating shorter flower stems for cafe tables from taller stems reserved for a weekend event.
Plover Reed Flowers grows decorative cut flowers on two rented acres and employs Sorn plus two seasonal workers.
Six cafes have standing orders totaling 900 stems a week during the agreed summer season.
The cafes pay 60 cents per delivered stem, making $540 in weekly gross receipts when all 900 contracted stems are supplied.
Event orders can pay $1.20 per stem but require more sorting by color and length and are not guaranteed each week.
Those prices are receipts before growing, labor, packing and delivery costs, not profit per stem.
The cafe agreements allow seasonal substitutions within a stated color range rather than requiring one flower variety every week.
Cafe customers can change quantities with seven days' notice, so a standing order is not a guaranteed year-round income.
The farm makes two cafe delivery rounds a week; the route takes approximately three hours each round.
Delivering many small bunches adds handling work that a single large collection order may not require.
Sorn sells additional mixed bouquets at the farm gate but has no commitment from passersby to buy surplus stems.
Sorn said, "The regular order tells me something about next week. It does not tell me what every bed will produce."
The farm recorded two weeks of substituted varieties after a crop bloomed later than expected; all six cafes accepted those substitutions.
That record does not establish that every future substitution will be accepted or that every event customer has similar flexibility.
Cafe owner Omi Holt prefers short stems that leave room for customers to see across small tables.
Holt said, "The arrangement has to leave space for lunch, not just look good before anyone sits down."
The farm has not produced a complete margin comparison between cafe, event and farm-gate sales channels.
Its seasonal workers are paid for packing and delivery preparation as well as cutting flowers.
A former potting shed serves as the packing room, with buckets marked for each cafe rather than individual diners.
The reporting record contains no quantified environmental comparison with imported flowers or promise that local flowers are available in every season.

forbidden_additions: $540 is weekly profit, higher event prices necessarily mean higher net margins or orders last all year
Universal acceptance of substitutions or quantified environmental advantages not measured
